title: Next Higher Integer With Same Set Bits
description: Given a positive integer `n`, return the smallest integer strictly greater than `n` that has the exact same number of `1`-bits in its binary representation.
hints: Isolate the lowest set bit with two's complement: `c = n & -n`. Adding `c` to `n` (`r = n + c`) turns the rightmost contiguous block of `1`-bits into `0`s and promotes the next `0` bit to `1`.
Gosper's hack restores the remaining `k - 1` ones from that block to the lowest bit positions in O(1): `(((r ^ n) >> 2) // c) | r`.

examples.explanation: 6 is 110 in binary (two 1s); the next higher integer with two 1s is 9 (1001).
12 is 1100 in binary (two 1s); the next higher integer with two 1s is 17 (10001).
1 is 1 in binary (one 1); the next higher integer with one 1 is 2 (10).
